name: The wolf's grave, a high pass in the Pilares
synopsis: Billy carries the dead wolf up into the Pilares and buries her and her unborn pups under a pile of loose rock in a high pass. He stays on in the mountains for weeks, shooting trout in the pools with a homemade bow and cane arrows, and hits a hawk that escapes with the arrow and is never found.

name: A promontory above the Bavispe
synopsis: Two days later Billy looks down from a high point on the Bavispe and it seems to be flowing the wrong way. He camps among junipers to see what the sunrise shows, and understands that he has crossed back over the range to the stretch where the river heads north.

name: El Tigre
synopsis: A week later, ragged and starving, Billy rides into this mining camp of a dozen mud houses. A woman feeds him beans and tortillas in her dark kitchen and brings out her sleeping sister, who touches his face and withdraws again. He leaves with no idea where he is going.

name: Among the Indians in the Sierras
synopsis: For days Billy lives among Indians in their mountain camps and caves. They feed him, wash and mend his clothes, stitch his boots, and warn him away from Yaqui country. As he leaves, an old man calls him an orphan and urges him to stop wandering, and Billy answers that he is not one.

name: The eastern escarpment above the Bavispe barranca
synopsis: Following a little-used wagon road east across the Sierras, Billy passes cairns for travellers killed long ago and reaches a rim of grey rock painted with old pictographs. He looks out over the Bavispe's barranca to the Carretas Plain, trims his horse's overgrown hooves, then spends some seven hours on the switchbacks down to the river.

name: Huisiachepic, the heretic's town
synopsis: Riding north along the river, Billy lets his bow drift away in a ford and crosses to a ruined town. Its only inhabitant, a pale former Mormon who keeps the church felled by the 1887 earthquake, cooks him eggs and tells him at length of a local man whose son died in that earthquake and who, in old age, camps in a ruined church to argue a case against God.

name: Tamichopa
synopsis: Billy rides north on a road that fords the river again and again, and passes through Tamichopa, a town the Apaches burned to the ground in 1758.

name: Bacerac
synopsis: A child leads Billy's horse into a courtyard where a burro turns a mill, and the household feeds him and gives him a cot, though he says nothing to anyone but thanks. In the morning he glimpses his father's horse passing in the street but can find no trace of it. Unable to find the women, he writes his thanks in flour on the table.

name: Bavispe
synopsis: Billy rides through Bavispe at midmorning without stopping, past a meat cart in the plaza by the church. It is the town where, in the heretic's tale, the earthquake killed the child.

name: Colonia Oaxaca (the alguacil's house)
synopsis: At noon Billy halts in the road outside the house of the alguacil who took the wolf from him, spits in the dust, and rides on.

name: Colonia Morelos
synopsis: Noon the next day Billy passes through Morelos again, the town where the wolf was put on show at the fair, on his way north to the border.

name: The road north towards Ojito
synopsis: Heading north under storm clouds that build all day, Billy fords the river one last time and is caught by hail in the low hills. He spends the night in an abandoned roadside compound and wakes late in the night to a still, moonlit plain under standing water.

name: The border at Douglas
synopsis: In the morning Billy rides through the border crossing into Arizona. He asks the guard, John Gilchrist, to lend him half a dollar for food, promises to send it back from Cloverdale, and the two agree that they like this country.

name: A pass in the Guadalupes on the old Cloverdale road
synopsis: After riding the old Douglas road all day, Billy reaches the pass at evening in a cold wind, reading names and dates cut into the rock by earlier travellers. Below lies the Animas Plain, and on the way down his horse knows where it is and hurries.

name: The Parham house
synopsis: Billy reaches home after midnight to find no horses, no dog and most of the furniture gone. He eats peaches from the pantry and sleeps on his own bed. Back from the Sanders' place next day, he drags the mattress off his parents' bed, finds a great dried bloodstain beneath it, and breaks down weeping.

name: Sanders' (the SK Bar)
synopsis: Billy rides north to the SK Bar, where old man Sanders, sitting on his porch, recognises neither him nor his horse. When Billy calls out his name, the old man summons his granddaughter Leona, who comes out and stands with a hand on his shoulder. What they tell Billy is not shown, but he rides back to the house half refusing to believe the old man.

name: Animas
synopsis: Billy finds the houses of Animas apparently empty. He fills his canteen at the tap beside the store without going in, then sleeps out on the open plain beyond the town with no food and no fire.

name: Lordsburg
synopsis: Billy rides into Lordsburg at noon the day after he finds the bloodstain, after a hungry night on the plain beyond Animas.

name: The Websters', Lordsburg
synopsis: The Websters' comes up only once, in passing, while Billy answers the sheriff's questions in his office elsewhere in town: it is where some of the Parham family's household goods have been taken.

name: Leaving the Websters', Lordsburg
synopsis: Billy finds Boyd at the Websters' house in the east of Lordsburg, and the mute dog greets him. The brothers take a shotgun and shells, nineteen dollars, a blanket, clothes and a sack of food, then ride out double over the highway and the Southern Pacific line, heading west.

name: Camp on the alkali flats
synopsis: They camp on the playa beside a fire of fenceposts the horse has dragged up, and in the dark Boyd says the killers called him by name. At sunrise one of Mr Boruff's riders comes across the shallow flood to question them, then turns back to report them as drifters.

name: Noon at the San Simon River
synopsis: Over the Arizona line and across a low range, they noon under cottonwoods by the river and sit naked in its shallow pool. Boyd has already warned Billy off questioning him, and when Billy asks whether one of the men wore their father's boots, Boyd gives him nothing more.

name: Across the highway east of Bowie
synopsis: Through the afternoon Boyd talks of California and Texas, asks why American law cannot follow them into Mexico and wants to know whether number five shot will kill a man. At evening they cross the highway on the east side of Bowie and take an old road south into the Dos Cabezas.

name: The old road through the Dos Cabezas
synopsis: They camp in the range, and Billy gathers wood along a shallow stony arroyo. By the fire he tells Boyd that what happened was no one's fault, but Boyd, with coyotes calling on the ridge to the north, says he has already driven himself crazy and seems weighed down by a grief Billy cannot reach.

name: Apache Pass
synopsis: Riding double, they top the pass on a sunny, windy day with ravens wheeling over the slopes. Billy shows Boyd where the colour of the land changes far to the south and tells him that is Mexico.

name: Elfrida
synopsis: At noon the next day they reach route 666 and follow the paved road down the Sulphur Springs Valley through Elfrida.

name: McNeal
synopsis: Still on route 666, they ride on south through McNeal towards the border.

name: Douglas
synopsis: In the evening they ride down the main street to the border gate. Gilchrist is off duty, so Billy leaves the half dollar he owes him with the other guard, recounting the coins Boyd hands him.

name: Agua Prieta
synopsis: They eat ice cream on the kerb while town dogs circle theirs, buy beans, meal, a pan and a pot, and change the last of their money into pesos. Then they follow the river out of town and camp in the desert, where Boyd admits to a bad feeling.

name: Ojito
synopsis: After a day along the stony riverbed they reach the hamlet in the early evening, hungry. A man in a doorway offers to sell them a chicken, and when they ride on a storm catches them on the empty road south just before dark.

name: Colonia Morelos at midnight
synopsis: Soaked by the storm, they ride through the town after midnight with Boyd asleep against Billy's back, wrapped in his brother's coat. They take the road south that Billy followed with the fairgoers last spring, and sleep until morning in a roadside jacal.

name: Bacerac
synopsis: A week into Mexico they find Keno tied outside a whitewashed house, wearing a Mexican saddle. Billy unsaddles him and sends Boyd off to hide with the horses, then slips into the house, where women are keeping watch over a dead woman and a tall, fair-haired foreigner comes out to meet him.

name: The eastern rim of the escarpment at sunrise
synopsis: Below Bacerac Billy tells Boyd the stranger is a German doctor with papers from a Casas Grandes broker, and they climb east on a track that dwindles to a footpath. After camps by a hillside farm and in an old burn, then two cold, wet days past ruined sawmills and a family working an old silver mine, they reach the eastern rim at sunrise above the Chihuahua plains.

name: The plains, with the Tarahumaras
synopsis: On the prairie below they spend a hungry night without a fire in a grove where cattle bed around a ciénega. In the morning vaqueros water their horses beside them, and a band of Tarahumaras on foot, heading back to the sierras, feed the brothers in silence before moving on.

name: Colonia Juárez
synopsis: Late in the afternoon they ride through the Mormon colony's orchards and vineyards, stuffing apples into their clothes. They cross the river on a narrow plank bridge and pass neat white houses with lawns and picket fences, and at the first bend the desert closes in again.

name: Casas Grandes
synopsis: Past the ruined mud city at dusk, they eat steak under electric light and sleep by the railway. Next day Gillian, of Soto y Gillian, shows Billy that Keno came in a lot of horses sold at auction by La Babícora, a ranch owned by Hearst, and urges the brothers to go home.

name: “The girl”, at a fire in an oak grove
synopsis: Riding south they pass a barefoot girl on the road, and when two riders go by in the dark the brothers turn back and find her at the men's fire. One man makes Billy drink mescal while Boyd stampedes their horses, and as Billy pulls “the girl” up behind him a knife slashes his boot and leg.

name: The Hacienda de San Diego
synopsis: After a dry camp where “the girl” makes them breakfast, they noon at a desert well and she rides on behind Boyd, asleep against his back. At evening they reach the hacienda on its hill above fields running to the Casas Grandes and Piedras Verdes rivers.
